title: Version lollipop special case (0, 127) may not match RFC 6550 intent
description:
## Location
rust/lichen-rpl/src/dodag.rs lines 76-79

## Issue
```rust
fn version_is_newer(new_ver: u8, old_ver: u8) -> bool {
    (new_ver, old_ver) == (0, 127)
        || lollipop_cmp(new_ver, old_ver) == Some(core::cmp::Ordering::Greater)
}
```

The special case `(0, 127)` hardcodes acceptance of version 0 as "newer" than version 127. Per RFC 6550 lollipop semantics:
- Linear region: 0-127 (sequential)
- Circular region: 128-255 (wrapping)

Version 127→0 is NOT a normal increment (linear region does not wrap). This special case may be intentional for DODAG restart scenarios but:
1. Not documented why this exception exists
2. Could allow version downgrade attacks if attacker sends version 0

## Test coverage
Line 955-960 tests this case but does not explain the rationale.

## Suggested action
Add comment explaining RFC basis for this special case, or verify against RFC 6550 section 7.2 whether this is correct behavior.
close_reason: The (0, 127) special case is already implemented at dodag.rs:90-93 with explicit test coverage in dodag_version_preserves_explicit_adjacent_restart_policy (lines 1115-1122). The test documents this as an intentional policy decision: lollipop_cmp(0,127) returns None per RFC literal text, but version_is_newer(0,127) returns true to handle the natural 127->0 wraparound in the circular region. The design decision was deliberately made and the RFC interpretation concern has been considered.
